name: You're Given a String...
problemStatement: You're given a string of lower-case Latin letters. Your task is to find the length of its longest substring that can be met in the string at least twice. These occurrences can overlap.
inputSpecification: The first input line contains the string. It's guaranteed, that the string is non-empty, consists of lower-case Latin letters, and its length doesn't exceed 100.
outputSpecification: Output one number — length of the longest substring that can be met in the string at least twice.

examples.title: Sample case 1: all unique characters
examples.why_included: This is the first sample case from the problem. With all unique characters, no substring can be repeated.

examples.title: Sample case 2: overlapping occurrences
examples.why_included: This is the second sample case. It specifically tests the requirement that occurrences can overlap ('aba' is found at index 0 and 2).

examples.title: Sample case 3: all same characters
examples.why_included: This is the third sample case. The longest repeated substring is 'zz' (length 2), which overlaps itself.

examples.title: Minimum length n=1
examples.why_included: Tests the minimum length constraint. A single character string has no substrings of length > 0 that can repeat.

examples.title: Minimum length n=2, repeated char
examples.why_included: The smallest string that has a repeating substring ('a', length 1).

examples.title: Minimum length n=2, unique chars
examples.why_included: The smallest string with no repeating characters.

examples.title: Simple non-overlapping case
examples.why_included: A basic case where the two halves of the string are identical and non-overlapping.

examples.title: String with all same characters
examples.why_included: For a string of length n with all identical characters, the answer is always n-1.

examples.title: Long string with all unique characters
examples.why_included: A longer string with no repeated substrings to confirm the base case.

examples.title: Repetition at start and end
examples.why_included: Tests finding a long, non-overlapping substring that appears at the beginning and end of the string.

examples.title: Repetition is internal to the string
examples.why_included: Tests when the longest repeated substring is not at the edges of the main string.

examples.title: Classic case: 'banana'
examples.why_included: A common string example. The longest repeated substrings are 'an' and 'na', both of length 2.

examples.title: Classic case: 'mississippi'
examples.why_included: Another common example. The longest repeated substring is 'issi' of length 4.

examples.title: Alternating two characters
examples.why_included: For a string (ab)*k, the longest repeated substring is (ab)*(k-1) of length 2k-2. Here, k=8, so length is 14.

examples.title: Alternating three characters
examples.why_included: For a string (abc)*k, the longest repeated substring is (abc)*(k-1) of length 3k-3. Here, k=6, so length is 15.

examples.title: Palindromic string with repeated center
examples.why_included: Tests a palindromic string where the longest repeated substring ('aba') is central to the structure and appears twice.

examples.title: Maximum length, all same characters
examples.why_included: Tests the maximum length constraint with the simplest repeating pattern. The answer should be n-1.

examples.title: Maximum length, constructed no repeats
examples.why_included: A max-length string constructed from repeated alphabets. The longest repeat is the full alphabet itself, length 26.

examples.title: Maximum length, alternating two characters
examples.why_included: A max-length string with a simple alternating pattern. The longest repeated substring is of length n-2.

examples.title: Maximum length, two identical halves
examples.why_included: A max-length string composed of two identical, non-overlapping 50-character substrings. The answer is exactly n/2.

examples.title: Maximum length, almost all same characters
examples.why_included: A max-length string that is almost entirely one character. The longest repeat is the block of 'a's of length n-2.

examples.title: Multiple competing repeated substrings
examples.why_included: Tests that the algorithm finds the globally longest substring ('pqpqpq', len 6) and isn't fooled by other shorter repeats ('abcde', len 5).

examples.title: Fibonacci-like string construction
examples.why_included: Strings built like Fibonacci numbers have complex overlapping structures. Here, 'abbab' of length 5 is the longest repeat.

examples.title: Long string with only single character repeats
examples.why_included: A string where many characters appear, but the only character that appears more than once is 'a'. The answer must be 1.

examples.title: Almost full string repeat by one char
examples.why_included: A string built from S and S' where S' is S without its last character. The answer is length(S) - 1.

examples.title: Length 99, alternating characters
examples.why_included: A known tricky case for alternating patterns of the form (ab...a). For length n=2k+1, the answer is n-2.

examples.title: Maximum length, all same characters
examples.why_included: Tests the maximum length constraint with the simplest repeating pattern. The answer should be n-1.

examples.title: Maximum length, two identical halves
examples.why_included: A max-length string composed of two identical, non-overlapping 50-character substrings. The answer is exactly n/2.

examples.title: Maximum length, alternating two characters
examples.why_included: A max-length string with a simple alternating pattern. The longest repeated substring is of length n-2.

examples.title: Maximum length, almost all same characters
examples.why_included: A max-length string that is almost entirely one character. The longest repeat is the block of 'a's of length n-2.

examples.title: Almost full string repeat by one char
examples.why_included: A string built from S and S' where S' is S without its last character. The answer is length(S) - 1.

examples.title: Length 99, alternating characters
examples.why_included: A known tricky case for alternating patterns of the form (ab...a). For length n=2k+1, the answer is n-2.

examples.title: Long repeat broken by one character
examples.why_included: Two long substrings are almost identical. A naive fuzzy matching algorithm might fail; the longest actual repeat is shorter.

examples.title: Overlapping repeat is the longest
examples.why_included: A case where the longest repeat ('abcdefgabcde') must be found via an overlapping match.

examples.title: Max length random, small alphabet
examples.why_included: Max length random string using only 'a'-'d'. Pigeonhole principle guarantees many repeats. Seed: 123.

examples.title: Max length random, large alphabet
examples.why_included: A max-length-like random string using a large alphabet, which tends to have shorter repeats. Seed: 456.

examples.title: Multiple distinct repeats of same max length
examples.why_included: Tests a string where two different substrings ('abc' and 'fgh') are repeated and share the same maximal length.

examples.title: Long prefix is also a suffix
examples.why_included: A string where a long prefix is also a suffix ('abracadabra'). This structure, called a border, is a classic stringology case.

examples.title: Only single character repetitions exist
examples.why_included: A string where no substring of length greater than 1 is repeated. The correct answer must be 1.

examples.title: Longest repeat has minimal length 2
examples.why_included: A string where the longest repeated substring ('xy') is short, ensuring the algorithm doesn't miss small candidates in a long string.

examples.title: Thue-Morse-like sequence with overlaps
examples.why_included: Sequences like this have complex, non-periodic overlapping structures. It's a good test for robust substring searching algorithms. The longest repeat is 'abaab'.

examples.title: Repeat is a block of same characters
examples.why_included: Tests that the algorithm correctly handles substrings that are themselves composed of a single repeated character. The longest is 'yyyyyy'.

examples.title: Overlapping repeat at the very beginning
examples.why_included: This case isolates an overlapping repetition ('aba') at the start of the string to check boundary conditions.

examples.title: Overlapping repeat at the very end
examples.why_included: Symmetric to the previous case, this one isolates an overlapping repetition ('aba') at the end of the string.

examples.title: Single character separating two long repeats
examples.why_included: Tests finding a long non-overlapping repeat where the two occurrences are adjacent, separated by just one character.

examples.title: Deceptive palindrome-like structure
examples.why_included: A string that is almost a palindrome of a single character. The longest repeat is the block of 49 'a's, not a longer substring involving 'X'.
